GRADES 3, 4 & 5 – Inter-House Scratch 3 Coding Competition

 

Learners of Grades 3, 4 and 5 will participate in an Inter-House Coding Competition using Scratch 3. They will demonstrate their programming skills and creativity by creating either a Game or a Story based on the topic assigned to them.

 

Qualifier Round

 

The preliminary rounds will be conducted during the week of 23–27 November for Grades 3, 4 and 5, during CTT or their scheduled Computing Lab lessons.

 

As per the competition format:

 

One learner from each house in every section will be shortlisted for the finale round.

The first runners-up (one per house per section) will also participate by supporting their respective house teams.

 

The selected learners will form their house teams and work collaboratively on their projects during CTT/Club lessons. They will have opportunities to discuss ideas, develop their projects and refine their creations.

 

Finalists will be selected based on a Debug Challenge. They will identify and fix bugs in a given Scratch program to achieve the desired output. Two fastest learners from each house in each section will qualify for the Finale.

 

Important Dates

27 November: Results for all grades will be announced. The topics and evaluation criteria for the final round will also be shared on Teams post selection of finalists.

7 December: Last date for submission of Scratch stories/games for review.

11 December: Informatico Concorso Finale – Final showcase of projects created and evaluation by judges.

Evaluation Criteria

 

The Scratch stories and games will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

 

Creativity and Originality: Uniqueness of the idea and creative use of sprites, backdrops and other elements.

Storyline / Game Design: Clarity, flow and engagement of the story or game, including its purpose and structure.

Programming Skills: Effective use of Scratch coding blocks, sequences, loops, events and other relevant programming concepts.

Functionality: Whether the scripts work correctly and the story/game performs as intended.

Overall Presentation: Quality, completeness and effectiveness of the final project.

 

House winners will be announced following the final evaluation.

 

Through this competition, learners will develop their creativity, collaboration, computational thinking and problem-solving skills while putting their coding knowledge into practice.

 

All the best,

Team-Computing

Dear Learners,

 

As discussed, please find below the details for your weekend project work, "Research and Make a Fossil."

Due Date for Submission: 12 Nov 2026

 

1. Research a Fossil

Choose one fossil and find out:

What was it?
Where was it found?
How old is it?
One interesting fact about it.

* Write your findings on an A4 sheet.

 

2. Write About Your Chosen Fossil

On the same A4 sheet, complete the following:

My fossil is: __________
It was found in: __________
It is approximately: __________ years old.
One interesting fact: __________
3. Make a Fossil Model
Use clay, dough, or any other suitable material.
Press a leaf, shell, toy, or another object into the material.
Carefully remove the object to create an impression.
Label your fossil model.

✨ You may research any fossil of your choice and create your fossil model using different materials or methods. Feel free to be creative!

 

Happy learning and fossil hunting! 🦴

Please note that your reading homework for today is uploaded under the 'Read and Reflect' module. 

How to access it:
Go to English Teams → go to the Classwork tab on the left side of your screen → open the "Read and Reflect" module.
Make sure to check this section every week and complete your weekly reading! 

 

This week's reading is the book Counting on Katherine: How Katherine Johnson saved Apollo 13

You've likely heard of the historic Apollo 13 moon landing. But do you know about the mathematical genius who made sure that Apollo 13 returned safely home? As a child, Katherine Johnson loved to count. She counted the steps on the road, the number of dishes and spoons she washed in the kitchen sink, everything! Boundless, curious, and excited by calculations, young Katherine longed to know as much as she could about math, about the universe. From Katherine's early beginnings as a gifted student to her heroic accomplishments as a prominent mathematician at NASA, this is the story of a groundbreaking American woman who not only calculated the course of moon landings but, in turn, saved lives and made enormous contributions to history.

 

Happy Reading!

The mighty Komodo dragon has razor-sharp teeth, powerful claws and incredible strength, while the deadly king cobra has lightning-fast reflexes and a venomous bite. The Primary Humanitas Fest – HUMANVERSE 2026, held today, was a wonderful celebration of learning, creativity and collaboration across Grades 2–5. We are delighted to share that our learners put up an excellent showcase of their Humanities learning through their creative displays, models and presentations.

It was truly inspiring to witness our young learners take ownership of their learning and demonstrate student agency at every step. Their enthusiasm and confidence were evident as they shared their ideas, made decisions, explored different possibilities and worked together as a team. Beyond the displays and presentations, what stood out was the learners' ability to think independently, collaborate purposefully, communicate their understanding and take pride in their work. Every effort reflected their curiosity, creativity, commitment and the joy of learning.

We would like to extend our heartfelt gratitude to all our parents for your encouragement, cooperation and support throughout the preparation for HUMANVERSE. Your involvement, motivation and willingness to support your children played a significant role in making this event a memorable experience. Thank you for giving our learners the confidence and encouragement to explore, create and express themselves.

The results of HUMANVERSE 2026 will be announced on 12 November 2026. We look forward to sharing the results with you!

As we celebrate the success of this event, we hope our learners carry forward the confidence, curiosity, teamwork and enthusiasm they demonstrated today into all their future learning experiences.

Thank you once again for being such an important part of our learning community and for helping us make HUMANVERSE 2026 a meaningful celebration of learning!

Warm regards,

Questions to Answer
1. What is the problem?

Describe the problem in 3-4 sentences.

2. Who is affected?

Explain who is impacted by this problem and how.

3. Who is responsible for addressing it?

Identify the people, community leaders, local authorities, or organizations responsible for solving the problem.

4. What action should be taken?

Suggest at least three practical actions that can help solve the problem.

5. How can community members participate?

Explain at least three ways community members can help improve the situation.

Answer Requirements

Write the title clearly.

Answer all five questions.

Write in complete sentences.

Include a coloured drawing or diagram related to your chosen community problem.

Use at least five Humanities vocabulary words from this unit (examples: community, responsibility, citizen, cooperation, leadership, participation, rules, laws).

Check your work for correct spelling and punctuation.

Success Criteria

I can:

Identify a community problem.

Explain who is affected by the problem.

Identify people responsible for addressing the issue.

Suggest practical solutions.

Explain how community members can work together to improve their community.
